title: security: POST /api/v1/security/explain with userId "" silently explains the caller instead of refusing
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcVkGJizGH7raJHhAvL

Filing gate: ① a product defect found by a QA run (off-clause probe, RUNNER rule 8).

## Reproduction
1. Boot the showcase: `objectstack dev --ui --seed-admin`. Sign in as admin@objectos.ai.
2. `POST /api/v1/security/explain` with body `{"object":"showcase_private_note","operation":"read","userId":"","recordId":"ID"}`, where ID is any showcase_private_note id.
3. Expected: a refusal (400 VALIDATION_FAILED, or the 404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND an unknown userId gets since #26641).
4. Actual: 200. The response explains the CALLER (principal = admin), not the user that was asked about.

## Mechanism
`security-plugin-explain-access.ts` (~L136) tests `if (request.userId && request.userId !== callerContext?.userId)`. An empty string is falsy, so the request skips the cross-user authorization branch and the `sys_user` existence check (~L174), and falls through to self-explain. The response does name the principal, so it does not mislead outright. But an explain asked about "nobody" answers about somebody else.

## Why it matters
A client that loses the selected user (an empty picker) gets a confident answer about the wrong principal. The unknown-id case was fixed by #26641; the empty-string case is the same door's remaining gap.
